clue.text: Match, perhaps, easier to pick up

definitions.meaning: a match is one example of a device for starting a flame, such as one used for a cigarette
comparative of the adjective meaning not heavy, so less effort to lift

explanation.surface: Someone weighing up whether a match is the handier thing to grab.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are the same spelling: a flame-making gadget, of which a match is an instance, and the comparative of 'not heavy'.

clue.text: French river, one entering mythology

indicators.note: one piece goes into the other

parts.note: lore is a body of traditional stories and beliefs
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A French river that has found its way into ancient myth.
explanation.definitionFit: The longest river in France, flowing west to the Atlantic past its chateaux.

clue.text: Descriptive of good food, ginormous starter massive

indicators.note: a word's starter is its first letter, with a nod to the first course of a meal

parts.note: astronomical means enormous, as in astronomical prices

explanation.surface: A food critic praising a huge first course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starter' fits the food picture as a first course but only supplies a first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective relates to gastronomy, the art of fine eating, so describes good food.

clue.text: Head of trade fit for the board

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: able means fit or capable, as in able-bodied

explanation.surface: A trade union leader judged suitable to sit on a company board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'board' looks like a committee but is a piece of furniture, and also meals provided, as in 'bed and board'.
explanation.definitionFit: Board is an old word for a dining surface, as in 'festive board'.

clue.text: Turn peeled potato into middle of tureen

indicators.note: the peeled letters are put inside the other pair
the middle of the word is its central letters
a peeled word loses its outer letters, like skin removed

explanation.surface: A cooking instruction to put a peeled potato into a soup bowl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'peeled' strips POTATO to OTAT, which goes 'into' RE, the middle of tureen.
explanation.definitionFit: To rotate is to turn round on an axis, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Fighting to swallow iron biscuit!

indicators.note: one word taking another into its middle, as a mouth swallows food

parts.note: fighting between nations is war
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

explanation.surface: A soldier in battle forced to gulp down a hard, metallic-tasting biscuit.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin crisp sweet biscuit, often served with ice cream, is called by this name.

clue.text: Strange brew in a drinking establishment

indicators.note: the letters come out in a strange, unfamiliar order

explanation.surface: An odd beer on offer in a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A bar specialising in wine is one type of place where people go to drink.

clue.text: Within the rules, blonde/fuddy-duddy partnership?

parts.note: fair hair is blonde hair
the joining word 'and' links two partners
a square is a dull, old-fashioned person

explanation.surface: A couple consisting of a blonde and a stuffy old bore.
explanation.walkthrough: The slash and 'partnership' show the two words are joined by 'and'.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means honestly and according to the rules, with nothing underhand.

clue.text: Ending in despair, two biblical characters help

indicators.note: the ending of a word is its last letter

parts.note: Eli was a priest in the Book of Samuel and Eve the first woman in Genesis

explanation.surface: Biblical figures offering assistance to someone at the end of their tether.
explanation.definitionFit: To relieve is to ease or assist someone in distress, so to help.

clue.text: Flimsy Italian buns thrown around street

indicators.note: the rearranged letters are placed round the street abbreviation
letters thrown about land jumbled, so these two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Light Italian bread rolls being tossed about in the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thrown' scrambles ITALIAN BUNS, and 'around' wraps those jumbled letters round ST.
explanation.definitionFit: Something flimsy lacks solidity or substance; the two words are close synonyms.

clue.text: Serious eastern winds

indicators.note: read as the verb (to wind, twist), so the word's letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A weather remark that the winds from the east are severe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'winds' looks like a noun for breezes, but it is the verb meaning twists.
explanation.definitionFit: An earnest person is sincere and solemn, a straightforward synonym of serious.

clue.text: Support leader in bitter contest

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: a race is a contest of speed

explanation.surface: Backing the frontrunner in a fiercely fought competition.
explanation.definitionFit: A brace is a support, such as a strut or a device holding teeth or a limb in place.

clue.text: Little bit of time

definitions.meaning: sixty seconds, a short spell (pronounced MIN-it)

explanation.surface: A plain phrase for a brief moment.
explanation.definitionFit: One spelling serves as an adjective meaning tiny and as a noun for sixty seconds, pronounced differently.

clue.text: Birds take issue with pastry dishes

parts.note: an issue of a periodical is a magazine, mag for short
pies are dishes baked in pastry

explanation.surface: Birds objecting to the pies on offer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take issue with' reads as a phrase for disagreeing; 'take' and 'with' are only links.
explanation.definitionFit: These black-and-white crows are an example of birds.

clue.text: Aintree desperate for apprentice

indicators.note: something desperate is in a wild state, so the word's letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Aintree racecourse, home of the Grand National, short of a young learner.
explanation.walkthrough: Aintree is the Liverpool racecourse where Britain's Grand National steeplechase is run.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words name someone learning a trade or job under supervision.

clue.text: Cooler close to cliff edge

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter

parts.note: a ridge is a narrow raised edge or crest

explanation.surface: Someone standing near the brink of a cliff, where it is chillier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cooler' reads as an adjective about the weather but is a noun here.
explanation.definitionFit: A cooler is a container or appliance for keeping things cold, which a refrigerator is.

clue.text: Dog — a figure following cat, initially

indicators.note: the article and the number come after the first letter
initially takes the first letter of the word

parts.note: nine is a figure, a number

explanation.surface: A dog trotting along behind a cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'following' puts A and NINE after C, the first letter of 'cat'.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun, it means any member of the dog family, so a dog.

clue.text: Written backwards in telegram, magical letter from Greece

indicators.note: Written backwards says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A spellbinding telegram composed in reverse, sent from Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points inside 'telegram, magical' for AMMAG, which 'Written backwards' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the third character of the Greek alphabet, so a letter from Greece.

clue.text: Old article, quite shabby

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: shabby means knocked about and run-down, so the word's letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A dealer's description of a worn-looking old piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'article' looks like an object for sale but is the grammatical article.
explanation.definitionFit: An adjective for something from a past era, typically valued for its age, so old.

clue.text: This crossword setter supports the idea

indicators.note: in a down entry the piece that supports another sits beneath it

parts.note: the setter refers to themselves as me

explanation.surface: The setter declaring backing for a concept.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the' sits in the surface as part of 'the idea' but gives its own letters; ME sits below it.
explanation.definitionFit: A theme is a central idea or subject running through a work.

clue.text: Competition level terrific at first

parts.note: even means level, as in an even surface

indicators.note: the first letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A contest that is splendid and evenly matched at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: A single contest in a sports programme, such as the 100 metres, is called by this name.

clue.text: Selfish Indian opener is a contender, surprisingly

indicators.note: the opener of a word is its first letter, as an opening batsman goes in first
the following words come out in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: A cricket remark that India's opening batsman is unexpectedly in the running.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opener' suggests a cricket opening batsman, but takes only the first letter of 'Indian'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being thoughtless of others' feelings is close in sense to being self-centred.

clue.text: Figure out, only about five

indicators.note: one word goes about, that is round, the other

parts.note: sole means only, as in sole survivor
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: Someone working out a sum with nothing more than five to go on.
explanation.definitionFit: To work out an answer or puzzle is to figure it out.

clue.text: Mountain always is found in France

parts.note: ever means always, as in ever hopeful
est is French for 'is'

explanation.surface: A claim that a certain peak is permanently located in France.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the world's highest peak, in the Himalayas, so an example of a mountain.
